_format_notes: THE ONTOLOGY - maps what a panicking bystander says to the Japanese a dispatcher expects.
REGISTER: polite (です/ます) throughout, founder's decision. NOTE the two 'reported' terms
(chest_pain, severe_abdominal_pain) are stored in PLAIN base form on purpose - the
'〜と言っています' wrapper added at render time makes them polite in the output. Every other
term is stored already-polite because it is stated directly.
Terms use plain everyday words, NOT medical register (息が苦しい, not 呼吸困難) - founder
FRAME - who the information comes from, clinically meaningful:
observed         - only the caller can know it (not breathing). Stated directly.
reported         - only the patient can know it (pain). Wrapped in 〜と言っています.
source_dependent - could be either; the Week-2 SLM resolves per utterance. For now the
crude matcher states them directly. Do not hard-code a frame guess.
verified: TRUE for all 29 - founder (fluent, resident in Japan) read every term and
confirmed each is natural, clear, non-diagnostic, and dispatcher-appropriate. The 13
added from the 緊急度判定プロトコル were reviewed 2026-08-12 as RENDERED OUTPUT (term +
frame wrapper), not as raw strings - that review is what caught the polite-form-before-
と言っています bug and the 脈がありません over-claim.

consciousness_states.japanese_term: 受け答えがおかしいです
consciousness_states.note: Founder kept this term. Means: their responses when spoken to are strange/off.

symptoms.note: Source-dependent: 'he says he can't breathe' (conscious) vs 'his breathing looks laboured' (observed). SLM resolves from phrasing.
Must never be missed or invented - drives CPR. Deliberately not 心肺停止 (diagnosis).
PLAIN base on purpose - wrapper -> 胸が痛いと言っています (polite in output).
Founder kept this term. Observable stroke sign - never 脳卒中.

symptoms.japanese_term: 呂律が回りにくいです
symptoms.note: Founder-verified term for slurred speech. です added for register consistency. Reintroduces the ろれつ sound (hard for a non-Japanese caller to say); Week-3 TTS mitigates this.

symptoms.japanese_term: 体の片側が動きません
symptoms.note: Avoided 片麻痺 as clinician language.
PLAIN base on purpose - wrapper -> お腹がすごく痛いと言っています (polite in output).
Most urgent in small children. Consider capturing an actual temperature separately.

symptoms._added: 2026-08-03 from 緊急度判定プロトコルVer.1 - CIRCULATION was missing entirely. Dispatchers assess THREE vital signs (呼吸/循環/意識); we only had breathing + consciousness. Both terms below are adapted from the protocol's own questions.
symptoms.japanese_term: 冷や汗をかいています
symptoms.note: CIRCULATION vital sign. Protocol asks 「冷や汗をかいていますか？」.
CIRCULATION vital sign. Protocol asks 「顔色は悪いですか？」.
Protocol lists 頭痛 as HIGH-URGENCY (緊急性が高い症候). Was missing.
Protocol lists 動悸 as HIGH-URGENCY. Their 通報内容: 「どきどきする」「動悸がする」.
Protocol lists 背部痛 as HIGH-URGENCY (aortic emergencies).
Protocol lists 腰痛 as HIGH-URGENCY.
Protocol lists めまい as a 症候. We previously treated 'dizzy' as out-of-scope - that was wrong.

OFFICIAL: protocol 通報内容 for 嘔気・嘔吐 is 「吐いた」「吐き気が強い」. This entry = actually vomiting (吐いた). Nausea-only is the separate `nausea` entry. ASPECT ASSUMPTION: 〜ています states this is ONGOING. If it already stopped the correct form is 吐いていました (founder-confirmed 2026-08-12). We cannot currently tell which - deliberate safe default, see the modifier-system entry in OPEN_DECISIONS.md.
OFFICIAL: protocol asks 「吐き気がありますか？」 and lists 「吐き気が強い」 in 通報内容. Deliberately separate from `vomiting` - saying 吐いています when they have only felt sick would fabricate a symptom.
Protocol lists しびれ as a 症候. Distinct from one_sided_weakness (can't move).
CPA keyword -> immediate R1 in the protocol.

symptoms.japanese_term: 体が冷たくなっています
symptoms.note: CPA keyword (冷たくなっている) -> immediate R1.

events.note_correction_2026_08_19: CORRECTED: 倒れる is CAUSE-NEUTRAL, not a medical-specific verb - it just means 'went down' and tells the dispatcher NOTHING about why. It is the right default ONLY when the caller gives no mechanism (sudden, unexplained). If a mechanism is stated, use `fall` or `fall_from_height` instead - do not use collapsed just because the cause sounds medical.

events.note: LEVEL-GROUND trip/slip only - falling from height is the separate `fall_from_height` entry below, because it is a different clinical picture (higher risk of spinal/multiple injury) and the crew needs to know which. 転倒 means 'lost balance and fell' but does NOT say from where, so it must not be used for a stairs/ladder fall. English 'fell' does not distinguish these on its own - the SLM reads the whole sentence, caller can correct on the confirmation screen. NEEDS FOUNDER CHECK.

A fall FROM HEIGHT (stairs, ladder, roof) carries materially higher risk of spinal or multiple injury than a level-ground trip, and the crew needs to know which they are walking into. 階段から落ちました is literally 'fell from the stairs' - it will read oddly for a ladder or roof fall. NEEDS FOUNDER CHECK: whether a more general term (例: 高い所から落ちました, 'fell from a height') should replace this so one term covers stairs/ladder/roof, or whether stairs specifically is common enough to keep as the default and add a second term for other heights.

events.japanese_term: のどに何か詰まっています

forms.finished: のどに何か詰まっていました

events.note: Usually observed, but a conscious patient may grab their throat and say it. Shortened from のどに物を詰まらせた for pronounceability.

forms.finished: けいれんしていました

events.note: ASPECT ASSUMPTION: 〜ています states this is ONGOING - clinically the sharpest case of this, since 'seizing now' and 'had one and stopped' drive different responses. Finished form would be けいれんしていました (mechanical 〜ています->〜ていました, NOT founder-checked). Safe default is ongoing: over-preparing the crew is harmless, under-preparing is not. See OPEN_DECISIONS.md.

events.japanese_term: 血がたくさん出ています

forms.finished: 血がたくさん出ていました

events.note: ASPECT ASSUMPTION: 〜ています states bleeding is ONGOING. Finished/controlled form would be 血がたくさん出ていました (mechanical, NOT founder-checked). Lower stakes than seizure - bleeding that has been stopped still matters to the crew. See OPEN_DECISIONS.md.
CPA keyword (水没) -> immediate R1 in the protocol. Bathtub drowning is a common domestic emergency in Japan.
